sentence: This project studies how three proteins that bind the HIV genome turn HIV expression up or down.
This project studies the neural mechanisms behind gait and mobility disturbances in preclinical dementia using digital biomarkers from videos.
This project builds a research infrastructure that supports investigators who answer questions where aging and cancer meet.
This project tests whether transcriptional changes in nerves and pathological tissues drive chronic low back pain in people having spine surgery.
This project studies how vaginal metabolites change with aging and whether they differ by race and ethnicity in the genitourinary syndrome of menopause.
This project uses single-cell whole-genome sequencing to map somatic mutations in normal mouse tissues during different life stages.
This project assesses gene-disease validity and makes public tools for interpreting genomic sequencing results from pregnancies with anomalies or pregnancy loss.
This project studies how an unstudied gene is involved in coronary disease, using cell and animal models of blood vessels.
This project builds technologies that link silent cancer mutations to splicing events and the protein isoforms they cause.
This project tests whether focused ultrasound guided by MRI can open the blood-brain barrier to help a molecule reach glioblastoma.
This project develops machine learning methods to speed up interventions for Alzheimer's Disease and related dementias, using electronic health record data for drug repurposing.
This project supports research into the causes and treatment of pancreatic cancer.
This project provides microscopes and imaging methods, such as confocal and multiphoton microscopy, to study living cells and organisms.
This project tests whether a wearable patch can map the electrical activity of the uterine surface during contractions in pregnancy.
This project studies how lymphocytes and their subtypes respond to proton radiation dose and linear energy transfer.
This project searches for general anesthetics that act on receptors regulating neurotransmission and studies how they work.
This project studies how social stress and protective factors affect alcohol use in Hispanic and white lesbian, gay, and bisexual youth.
This project builds data and technology support for stillbirth research, including a biorepository, harmonized data and artificial intelligence methods.
This project studies how viscoelastic materials change the tiny forces that receptors feel and tries to engineer receptor forces that ignore viscoelasticity.
This project develops a base editing treatment using lipid nanoparticles to correct nonsense mutations that cause cystic fibrosis.
